statement:
Assume full AC. Put $\mathcal A_r=\{x\in\mathbb R^4:r/2<|x|<2r\}$, with Euclidean coefficient and Frobenius matrix norms. There are universal $\delta,C>0$ such that every smooth $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ connection form $A$ near $\overline{\mathcal A_r}$ with
$$r^2\|F_A\|_{L^\infty(\mathcal A_r)}\le\delta$$
has a smooth gauge $g:\mathcal A_r\to SU(2)$ satisfying
$$\|A^g\|_{L^\infty(\mathcal A_r)}\le Cr\|F_A\|_{L^\infty(\mathcal A_r)},\qquad A^g=g^{-1}dg+g^{-1}Ag.$$
No Coulomb condition or gauge bound from a curvature $L^2$ norm alone is asserted here.

steps.text: **Constructed transport and its exact variation.** For a smooth path $H(s,t)$ use [F1] to construct $U(s,t)\in SU(2)$ with $\partial_tU=-a_tU$, $U(s,0)=I$, where $a_t=A(H)(\partial_tH)$ and $a_s=A(H)(\partial_sH)$. Direct differentiation gives $\partial_t\{U^{-1}(\partial_sU+a_sU)\}=U^{-1}F_{ts}U$, where $F_{ts}=\partial_ta_s-\partial_sa_t+[a_t,a_s]=F_A(H)(\partial_tH,\partial_sH)$. Integrating from zero to one yields $\partial_sU(s,1)+a_s(s,1)U(s,1)-U(s,1)a_s(s,0)=U(s,1)\int_0^1U(s,t)^{-1}F_{ts}U(s,t)\,dt$. In particular, when the initial point is fixed, the covariant derivative of the endpoint transport in direction $s$ has norm at most $\int_0^1|F_A(H)(\partial_tH,\partial_sH)|\,dt$. When both endpoints are fixed, integration also gives $|U(s_1,1)-U(s_0,1)|\le\int_{s_0}^{s_1}\int_0^1|F_A(H)(\partial_tH,\partial_sH)|\,dt\,ds$. For piecewise smooth path families these formulas hold piecewise and add: the intermediate $a_s$ terms cancel since the path and its $s$ derivative match at the joins. Uniqueness also gives reversal and concatenation, with later path transports multiplying on the left. [F1, given, construct, algebra]

**Two spherical path families with bounded variation.** Fix orthogonal unit vectors $N,E\in\mathbb R^4$, and put $S=-N$. For $x=\rho\omega\in\mathcal A_1$, the northern family goes from $N$ along the short spherical geodesic on the unit sphere to $\omega$, then radially to $\rho\omega$. Use it on $U_N=\{\omega\cdot N>-1/\sqrt2\}$. The southern family first follows the fixed semicircle $N\to E\to S$, then the short spherical geodesic from $S$ to $\omega$, then the same radial segment. Use it on $U_S=\{\omega\cdot N<1/\sqrt2\}$. All paths stay in the closed annulus. Their variable geodesic pieces are smooth in $x$, including their centers: the formula $\cos(t\theta)N+(\sin(t\theta)/\sin\theta)(\omega-\cos\theta N)$, $\theta=\arccos(\omega\cdot N)<3\pi/4$, has the removable smooth value at $\theta=0$ by its power series in $\theta^2$. On these fixed caps the parameter derivatives in an endpoint direction $v$ are bounded by $C|v|$, and the integrated path speeds are bounded by $C$, since $1/2<\rho<2$; the same holds with $N$ replaced by $S$. Construct their endpoint transports $q_N,q_S$ by [F1]. Applying the first-endpoint-fixed formula of step 1.1 gives $|dq_N+Aq_N|\le CL$ and $|dq_S+Aq_S|\le CL$. Hence $|A^{q_N}|,|A^{q_S}|\le CL$ on their respective domains. No bound on $A$ itself was used. [F1, step 1.1, construct, algebra]

**Curvature controls the relative frame on the overlap.** Let $\omega$ lie in the overlap. The common radial transports cancel in $h=q_N^{-1}q_S$. The two angular paths differ by the spherical loop $N\to E\to S\to\omega\to N$. Write $\omega=\cos\theta N+\sin\theta w$ with $w\perp N$, $|w|=1$. Choose a shortest great-circle arc $w(s)$ in the unit sphere of $N^\perp$ joining $E$ to $w$; its length is at most $\pi$ (when the endpoints are antipodal, choose any perpendicular intermediate direction). The homotopy $H(s,t)=\cos(\pi t)N+\sin(\pi t)w(s)$ has fixed endpoints $N,S$ and sweeps a spherical lune with area at most $2\pi$, since $|\partial_sH\wedge\partial_tH|=\pi\sin(\pi t)|w'(s)|$. The fixed-endpoint formula of step 1.1 bounds the difference of the two semicircle transports by $2\pi L$. The second semicircle passes through $\omega$; multiplying by its remaining reversed segment and using unitarity identifies this difference with $|q_N-q_S|$. Therefore $|h-I|\le2\pi L$ throughout the overlap. This argument needs only a homotopy for each fixed $\omega$, not a smoothly chosen family of lune fillings as $\omega$ varies. [step 1.1, step 2.1, choose, construct, algebra]

**A genuine global SU(2) frame by averaging.** Choose a smooth angular weight $\phi_N$ equal to zero for $\omega\cdot N\le-1/2$ and to one for $\omega\cdot N\ge1/2$, with $0\le\phi_N\le1$ and $|d\phi_N|\le C$ on the annulus; put $\phi_S=1-\phi_N$. Its supports lie inside the corresponding caps and the derivative is supported on their overlap. Form $T=\phi_Nq_N+\phi_Sq_S$, interpreting each weighted summand as zero outside its cap. On the overlap, $q_N^{-1}T=\phi_NI+\phi_Sh$ has distance at most $2\pi L$ from $I$; outside it $T$ is the one available unitary frame. Choose $\delta$ so that $2\pi\delta<1/2$. Every $SU(2)$ matrix, and hence $T$, belongs to the real quaternionic matrix space $\{\left(\begin{smallmatrix}\alpha&\beta\\-\overline\beta&\overline\alpha\end{smallmatrix}\right)\}$. Direct multiplication gives $T^*T=\lambda^2I$ and $\det T=\lambda^2$, where $\lambda=(\tfrac12\operatorname{tr}T^*T)^{1/2}>1/2$. Thus $g=T/\lambda$ is a globally smooth $SU(2)$ frame on the annulus. [F2, step 2.1, step 3.1, choose, construct, algebra]

**The gauge estimate survives normalization.** Put $D_AT=dT+AT$. The product rule gives $D_AT=(d\phi_N)(q_N-q_S)+\phi_N(dq_N+Aq_N)+\phi_S(dq_S+Aq_S)$ where both frames are present, with its evident one-frame form elsewhere. Steps 2.1–3.1 imply $|D_AT|\le CL$. The large original coefficient $A$ cancels from the derivative of the scalar norm: since $A^*=-A$, differentiating $\lambda^2=\tfrac12\operatorname{tr}T^*T$ gives the same expression with $dT$ replaced by $D_AT$, so $|d\lambda|\le C|D_AT|\le CL$ using the fixed upper and lower bounds on $\lambda$. Consequently $|D_Ag|=|\lambda^{-1}D_AT-\lambda^{-2}T\,d\lambda|\le CL$. Unitarity now gives $|A^g|=|g^{-1}D_Ag|\le CL$ on the whole annulus. The angular holonomy estimate, not an unproved radial critical estimate, is what permits this global averaging. [step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, algebra]

**Scaling and conclusion.** For general $r$, pull back by $y\mapsto ry$ to obtain $A_r(y)=rA(ry)$ with $\|F_{A_r}\|_\infty=r^2\|F_A\|_\infty\le\delta$. Apply steps 1.1–5.1 and define the physical gauge by $g(x)=g_r(x/r)$. Since $(A_r)^{g_r}(y)=rA^g(ry)$, the unit-annulus estimate becomes $\|A^g\|_\infty\le Cr\|F_A\|_\infty$. All constructions are smooth on the stated annulus, and full AC is inherited only through the explicitly used supplier context. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 5.1, construct, algebra] ∎
